title: Baynook Parking Booking
outcome: Live: staff claim a free bay in two clicks, and the database makes a double booking impossible.
summary: An office with a fixed pool of numbered bays needs a fair, simple way to share them. Staff see which bays are free by day, week or on a map, claim one and add it to their calendar. Admins manage bays, people, fixed holders and rules, and reception gets a read-only board of who parks where.
cv: Product built for mttn (Mitten Digital Solutions LLC), running as a public demo with one-click Staff, Admin and Reception sign-in.

cards.title: Architecture
cards.caption: A React app and Netlify Functions on one origin over Postgres on Neon. Sessions are a signed cookie the browser never reads, and the app calls no other site.
cards.alt: Architecture diagram: three roles, React single-page app, Netlify Functions and Postgres on Neon, the rules guaranteed by design and the outputs

cards.title: No double bookings, by design
cards.caption: The two hard rules live in the database. If two people click the same bay at once, exactly one wins; the app turns the other into a clear message.
cards.code:
-- Rule 1: a bay can hold at most one live booking on a date.
create unique index bookings_space_date_live_idx
  on bookings (space_id, booking_date) where status <> 'cancelled';
-- Rule 2: one live booking per user per date FOR THEMSELVES.
create unique index bookings_user_date_live_idx
  on bookings (user_id, booking_date)
  where status <> 'cancelled' and booked_for = 'self';

cards.title: Engineering discipline
cards.caption: Counted from the repository: unit, API and end-to-end tests (Vitest and Playwright), Netlify Functions and database migrations. Fonts are self-hosted, so the app loads nothing from other sites.

description.text: Silent, 7 seconds. 0:00 A staff member is on Book a bay, day view, with free bays outlined and taken bays filled in with colleagues' names. 0:02 The pointer moves to bay 120, which is free, and clicks it. 0:03 A side panel opens for bay 120 with the date and a choice to book it for myself or a visitor. 0:05 The pointer clicks Confirm booking. 0:06 A confirmation page reads Bay booked, shows bay 120 and the date, and offers Add to calendar.

cards.title: Built with Claude Code
cards.body: Built with Claude Code from a written brief. The repo keeps its agent instructions, architecture notes and changelog, and a change is only done once types check and the relevant unit, API or end-to-end tests pass.
